data.name: Primary Efficacy Objective
data.text: To demonstrate that 3 mg LY900018 is non-inferior to 1 mg IMG for the proportion of patients achieving treatment success from insulin-induced hypoglycemia using a non-inferiority margin of 10%

data.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Objective
data.text: To compare the safety and tolerability of 3 mg LY900018 with 1 mg IMG

data.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Objective
data.text: To characterize the PK profile of 3 mg LY900018 compared to 1 mg IMG

data.name: Secondary Pharmacodynamic Objective
data.text: To characterize the PD profile of 3 mg LY900018 compared to 1 mg IMG

data.name: Exploratory Anti-glucagon Antibody Objective
data.text: Explore the formation of anti-glucagon antibodies to glucagon

data.name: Exploratory Hypoglycemia Recovery Objective
data.text: To evaluate the recovery from clinical symptoms of hypoglycemia

data.name: Primary Efficacy Endpoint
data.text: The proportion of patients achieving treatment success defined as either an increase in PG to >70 mg/dL or an increase of >20 mg/dL from nadir within 30 minutes after administration of glucagon. The nadir is defined as the minimum PG value at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration.

data.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Endpoint
data.text: SAE, TEAEs (including gastrointestinal, nasal, and non-nasal AEs), vital signs

data.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Endpoint
data.text: PK parameters include AUC, Cmax, Tmax

data.name: Secondary Pharmacodynamic Endpoint
data.text: PD parameters include BGmax and Tmax

data.name: Primary Efficacy Estimand: Non-inferiority of LY900018 vs IMG for Treatment Success
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who undergo controlled insulin-induced hypoglycemia and complete both treatment periods with evaluable primary outcome. Patients are excluded if the lowest PG concentration at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration is ≥70 mg/dL, or if they receive an external measure to raise PG concentration either before glucagon administration or within the first 10 minutes of glucagon administration. (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, restricted to completers with evaluable primary outcome in both periods) Summary measure: Difference in proportions (percentages) of treatment success between IMG and LY900018 (IMG minus LY900018), with a 2-sided 95% confidence interval derived from the 1-sample mean of paired differences in primary outcome across 2 treatment visits. Non-inferiority declared if the upper limit of the 2-sided 95% CI is less than the non-inferiority margin of 10%..

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of additional intervention to raise plasma glucose before or within 10 minutes of glucagon administration
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives an external measure (e.g., IV glucose infusion) to raise PG concentration either before glucagon administration or within the first 10 minutes of glucagon administration, which would confound the assessment of glucagon treatment success.

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of IV glucose infusion after glucagon administration to prevent progression to severe hypoglycemia
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives IV glucose infusion after glucagon administration (beyond the first 10 minutes) to prevent progression to severe hypoglycemia. Data collected after IV glucose infusion may be excluded from the primary efficacy analysis.

intercurrentEvents.name: Non-evaluable primary outcome due to insufficient hypoglycemia induction
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient has a lowest PG concentration at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration of ≥70 mg/dL, rendering the primary outcome non-evaluable as the hypoglycemia threshold was not achieved prior to glucagon administration.

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before completing both treatment periods
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues the study before completing both treatment periods with evaluable primary outcome for any reason (e.g., adverse event, withdrawal of consent, protocol deviation). Such patients are excluded from the primary efficacy analysis and may be replaced.

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single nasal dose by study site personnel compared to 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen, Novo Nordisk A/S) administered as a single IM injection by study site personnel, in a 2-period crossover design
data.analysisPopulation: Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, restricted to completers with evaluable primary outcome in both periods
data.variableOfInterest: The proportion of patients achieving treatment success defined as either an increase in plasma glucose (PG) to ≥70 mg/dL or an increase of ≥20 mg/dL from PG nadir within 30 minutes after administration of glucagon, without receiving additional treatments to increase PG. The nadir is defined as the minimum PG value at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration.
data.summaryMeasure: Difference in proportions (percentages) of treatment success between IMG and LY900018 (IMG minus LY900018), with a 2-sided 95% confidence interval derived from the 1-sample mean of paired differences in primary outcome across 2 treatment visits. Non-inferiority declared if the upper limit of the 2-sided 95% CI is less than the non-inferiority margin of 10%.

data.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Estimand: LY900018 vs IMG
data.populationSummary: All enrolled Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who received at least one dose of study treatment, regardless of whether they completed all protocol requirements. (Safety Population - all enrolled patients whether or not they completed all protocol requirements) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics including incidence rates (counts and percentages) of TEAEs and SAEs by treatment group, and descriptive summaries of vital signs parameters by treatment group and time point..

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of rescue intervention for severe hypoglycemia
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives IV glucose or other rescue intervention for severe hypoglycemia during the study procedure, which may confound the safety profile attributable to the study treatment.

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation due to adverse event
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues the study due to an adverse event before completing all assessments. All AEs leading to discontinuation are captured and included in the safety analysis.

intercurrentEvents.name: Concomitant medication use
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient uses concomitant medications during the study period that may affect the safety profile or vital signs assessments.

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single nasal dose compared to 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen, Novo Nordisk A/S) administered as a single IM injection, in a 2-period crossover design
data.analysisPopulation: Safety Population - all enrolled patients whether or not they completed all protocol requirements
data.variableOfInterest: Incidence and severity of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) including gastrointestinal AEs, nasal AEs, and non-nasal AEs; serious adverse events (SAEs); and changes in vital signs following single-dose administration.
data.summaryMeasure: Descriptive statistics including incidence rates (counts and percentages) of TEAEs and SAEs by treatment group, and descriptive summaries of vital signs parameters by treatment group and time point.

data.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Estimand: LY900018 vs IMG
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who were randomized and received at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, with evaluable PK samples. (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, with sufficient PK sampling data) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, geometric mean, median, minimum, maximum) of PK parameters by treatment group. Comparative summaries between LY900018 and IMG..

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of IV glucose infusion affecting glucagon PK assessment
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives IV glucose infusion during the PK sampling window, which may affect glucagon absorption or distribution and confound PK parameter estimation.

intercurrentEvents.name: Missing or insufficient PK samples
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient has missing or insufficient blood samples for PK parameter estimation due to sampling issues, patient non-compliance, or early discontinuation.

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before completion of PK sampling
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues the study or a treatment period before completion of the 4-hour post-dose PK sampling window.

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single nasal dose compared to 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen, Novo Nordisk A/S) administered as a single IM injection, in a 2-period crossover design with serial blood sampling immediately before and up to 4 hours post-dose
data.analysisPopulation: Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, with sufficient PK sampling data
data.variableOfInterest: Pharmacokinetic parameters derived from glucagon plasma concentration-time profiles following single-dose administration, including area under the concentration-time curve (AUC), maximum observed plasma concentration (Cmax), and time to maximum concentration (Tmax).
data.summaryMeasure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, geometric mean, median, minimum, maximum) of PK parameters by treatment group. Comparative summaries between LY900018 and IMG.

data.name: Secondary Pharmacodynamic Estimand: LY900018 vs IMG
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who were randomized and received at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, with evaluable PD (plasma glucose) measurements. (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, with evaluable PD data) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, maximum) of PD parameters (BGmax and Tmax) by treatment group, along with descriptive summaries of plasma glucose values at baseline and various post-dose time points and absolute change from baseline..

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of additional intervention to raise plasma glucose after glucagon administration
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives IV glucose infusion or other intervention to raise PG concentration after glucagon administration. Measurements taken after the time of intervention will be excluded from the PD analysis.

intercurrentEvents.name: Carbohydrate-rich meal administration prior to discharge
intercurrentEvents.text: All patients receive a carbohydrate-rich meal prior to discharge, which may affect plasma glucose measurements in the later post-dose period.

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before completion of PD sampling
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues the study or a treatment period before completion of the post-dose PD sampling window, resulting in incomplete plasma glucose profiles.

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single nasal dose compared to 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen, Novo Nordisk A/S) administered as a single IM injection, in a 2-period crossover design with serial plasma glucose measurements immediately before and up to 4 hours post-dose
data.analysisPopulation: Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, with evaluable PD data
data.variableOfInterest: Pharmacodynamic parameters derived from plasma glucose concentration-time profiles following single-dose glucagon administration, including maximum plasma glucose concentration (BGmax) and time to maximum plasma glucose concentration (Tmax).
data.summaryMeasure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, maximum) of PD parameters (BGmax and Tmax) by treatment group, along with descriptive summaries of plasma glucose values at baseline and various post-dose time points and absolute change from baseline.

data.name: Exploratory Anti-glucagon Antibody Estimand
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who were randomized and received at least one dose of investigational product, with available antibody samples at baseline and follow-up. (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product with evaluable anti-glucagon antibody samples) Summary measure: Descriptive summary of the proportion of patients with detectable anti-glucagon antibodies by treatment group..

intercurrentEvents.name: Missing follow-up antibody sample
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient does not attend the follow-up visit or does not provide a blood sample for anti-glucagon antibody assessment 26 to 30 days after the last study treatment.

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before follow-up visit
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues the study before the follow-up visit, precluding assessment of anti-glucagon antibody formation.

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single nasal dose compared to 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen, Novo Nordisk A/S) administered as a single IM injection, assessed at follow-up visit 26 to 30 days after the last study treatment
data.analysisPopulation: Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product with evaluable anti-glucagon antibody samples
data.variableOfInterest: Presence or absence of anti-glucagon antibodies following single-dose administration of LY900018 or IMG, assessed at the follow-up visit (26 to 30 days after last study treatment).
data.summaryMeasure: Descriptive summary of the proportion of patients with detectable anti-glucagon antibodies by treatment group.

data.name: Exploratory Hypoglycemia Symptoms Recovery Estimand
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who were randomized and received at least one dose of investigational product, with evaluable hypoglycemia symptom questionnaire data. (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product with evaluable hypoglycemia symptom questionnaire data) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, maximum) of total score and each subscale score of the Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Scale at baseline, various post-dose time points, and absolute change from baseline by treatment group..

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of additional intervention to raise plasma glucose
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives IV glucose or other rescue intervention for hypoglycemia, which may independently alleviate hypoglycemia symptoms and confound the assessment of glucagon-mediated symptom recovery.

intercurrentEvents.name: Missing or incomplete hypoglycemia symptom questionnaire
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient does not complete the hypoglycemia symptoms questionnaire at one or more scheduled time points due to symptom severity, early discontinuation, or other reasons.

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before completion of symptom assessments
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues the study or a treatment period before completing all scheduled hypoglycemia symptom questionnaire assessments.

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single nasal dose compared to 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen, Novo Nordisk A/S) administered as a single IM injection
data.analysisPopulation: Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product with evaluable hypoglycemia symptom questionnaire data
data.variableOfInterest: Recovery from clinical symptoms of hypoglycemia as assessed by the Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Scale questionnaire, including total score and each subscale score at baseline and various post-dose time points.
data.summaryMeasure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, maximum) of total score and each subscale score of the Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Scale at baseline, various post-dose time points, and absolute change from baseline by treatment group.
